setup.https.title: Set up encryption
setup.https.intro: Before you choose a password, your box gets a secure connection (HTTPS). No service outside your home is needed for this.
setup.https.hint: The box creates a certificate that is valid only for this box's own name and for no other website. The name you are using to reach the box right now:
setup.https.invalidhost: This address cannot be used for HTTPS. Open the box by its IP address or a name like hejmo.local.
setup.https.public.title: Public name (recommended)
setup.https.public.hint: Your box gets a name such as familie.dedyn.io that points to its address at home, and a certificate every phone and browser trusts without installing anything. Only the name and a few checks leave your home; your data stays on the box.
setup.https.public.name: Name of the box
setup.https.public.token.hint: Create a free account and a name at deSEC (desec.io), then create an access token there. The token is stored encrypted on the box.
setup.https.public.lan_ip: Address of the box at home
setup.https.public.email: Email address for the certificate authority (optional; enables the ZeroSSL fallback)
setup.https.public.actalis.hint: Actalis needs a free account; enter the key ID and HMAC key it shows you.
setup.https.public.terms: By continuing you accept the terms of the chosen certificate authority.
setup.https.public.invalid: Please check the name, the token, the address and, for Actalis, the account keys.
setup.https.public.failed: The box could not get the certificate. Check the token and the name at deSEC, then try again. The box log has the details.
setup.https.check.title: Check the name
setup.https.check.intro: Your browser now tests whether it can reach the box under its new name:
setup.https.rebind.title: Your router blocks the name
setup.https.rebind.why: The name points to an address inside your home. Many routers, such as the FRITZ!Box, refuse such answers by default (DNS rebind protection). Add an exception for the name:
setup.https.rebind.step1: On the FRITZ!Box, open Home Network > Network > Network Settings > Additional Settings > Home Network.
setup.https.rebind.step2: Under DNS rebind protection, add this name to the host name exceptions:
setup.https.rebind.step3: Apply the change. This page checks again every few seconds.
setup.https.ownca.title: Cannot change the router?
setup.https.ownca.text: Use the box's own certificate authority instead. The public name is forgotten; you then install the box's certificate on each device.
setup.https.rebind.other: With other routers, look for DNS rebind protection or a list of allowed names.
trust.title: Trust the box
trust.intro: So that your devices trust the box, install its certificate once. It is valid for the box itself only.
trust.ios.title: iPhone and iPad
trust.ios.steps: Download the profile, install it under "Profile Downloaded" in Settings, then enable it under Settings > General > About > Certificate Trust Settings.
trust.android.title: Android and DAVx5
trust.android.steps: When DAVx5 first connects, it asks whether to trust the box's certificate: confirm once. Other Android apps need the certificate installed as a CA certificate in the security settings and often still do not trust it.
trust.mac.title: Mac
trust.mac.steps: Download the certificate, open Keychain Access and select the "login" keychain in the sidebar. Drag hejmo-ca.crt into it (or use File > Import Items and choose "login"). Double-click "Hejmo box CA", expand "Trust" and set "When using this certificate" to "Always Trust". Close the window and confirm with your Mac password. Double-clicking the file in Downloads is not enough: error -25294 means the wrong keychain was chosen, so use "login".
trust.browser.title: Windows, Linux and Firefox
trust.browser.steps: Download the certificate and import it as a trusted certificate authority in the operating system (Windows, Linux; Chrome, Edge) or in Firefox's certificate settings.
trust.fingerprint: SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate, to compare on your device:

connections.title: iCloud and CalDAV
connections.add: Connect iCloud or another CalDAV server
connections.hint: For other servers enter the full CalDAV address (Nextcloud: https://your-server/remote.php/dav). For iCloud use your Apple ID and an app-specific password from appleid.apple.com. Removing a connection removes its calendars from the box and deletes nothing at iCloud or on the server.

https.warning: The box's HTTPS certificate could not be renewed or loaded. Devices will refuse to connect once it has expired or is missing.
https.warning.hint: Check the DNS token and that the box is online; it tries again automatically. If the certificate authority or deSEC cannot be reached, waiting helps; if the key file secret.key was lost, restore it from your backup. Until then the box may serve its own certificate: install the box certificate on the phones (page /ca) so they trust it.
caldav.title: Calendar apps
caldav.intro: Phones and calendar apps (iOS Calendar, DAVx5 and others) can subscribe to the box's calendars and save events back. Add a calendar account of type CalDAV with the address and user name below. As the password, use a device token created here: one per device, revoked on its own.
caldav.tokens.none: No passwords for phones or calendar apps yet.
caldav.token.name: Device name, for example "iPhone Mama"
caldav.token.once: Enter this token as the password in the calendar app now. It is shown only once; if it is lost, revoke it and create a new one.
caldav.calendars.intro: The family calendar is always available. Subscribed calendars are shared through the box if you switch it on; calendars from other services are better added on the phone directly.
caldav.profile.title: Set up an iPhone or iPad in one step
caldav.profile.intro: Download an iPhone profile that sets up the calendar account for you: server address, your user name and a new device token are inside. Open the file directly on the iPhone or iPad, install it under "Profile Downloaded" in Settings, and delete the file afterwards.
caldav.profile.ca_first: Your box uses its own certificate: install the box's certificate profile on the device first.
caldav.profile.once: The box keeps no copy. The file holds the token in plain text; to get one again, create a new profile, which creates a new token. Removing the profile on the device does not revoke the token: do that under Device tokens.
caldav.profile.error.https: The profile holds a password and is only offered over HTTPS. Open the box through its HTTPS address.
